newsitem.title: CANADA: Fletcher Canada workers vote to strike.
newsitem.headline: Fletcher Canada workers vote to strike.

text.p: Unionized workers at Fletcher Challenge Canada Ltd's three pulp and paper mills in British Columbia voted 96 percent in favor of a strike, although no strike date was set, one of the workers' two unions said on Tuesday.
The Communications, Energy and Paperworkers Union said in a statement that the results sent a "strong message" to Fletcher that the company must make concessions to avoid a work disruption.
The union said it hoped that negotiations, which collapsed last week, would resume soon.
The unions said previously that the talks broke down over the company's demand for an eight-year contract. The unions had offered a three-year deal.
Fletcher Canada is majority owned by New Zealand's Fletcher Challenge Ltd. The workers' previous contract expired on April 30.
